questions.question: Which of the following metals is more reactive towards dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnesium (Mg) is more reactive towards dilute hydrochloric acid compared to aluminum (Al), zinc (Zn), and iron (Fe).
 
• When magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, it produces hydrogen gas and forms magnesium chloride:
 
• {Mg} + 2{HCl} rightarrow {MgCl}₂ + {H}₂ 
 
• This reaction is faster and more vigorous than the reactions of Al, Zn, and Fe with dilute hydrochloric acid.
 
• Magnesium is higher in the reactivity series compared to aluminum, zinc, and iron, making it more reactive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a series of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity.
 
• It helps to predict how metals will react with acids, water, and other substances.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas Test**
 
 
• Hydrogen gas can be tested by bringing a lit splint near the mouth of the test tube; a 'pop' sound confirms the presence of hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **Reactions of Other Metals**
 
 
• Aluminum reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form aluminum chloride and hydrogen gas, but it is less vigorous due to the formation of a protective oxide layer.
 
• Zinc reacts more readily than iron but less than magnesium, forming zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.
 
• Iron reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form iron(II) chloride and hydrogen gas, but the reaction is slower compared to magnesium and zinc.

questions.question: Which of the following is the major constituent of the liquefied petroleum gas?
questions.solution:
The correct option is **Butane**.

__**EXPLANATION**__:

__
 
• The gas, which we use in our home for the preparation of food is called liquid petroleum gas.
 
• The main constituents of LPG are the liquid form of butane and isobutane.
 
• Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) is a combination of propane and butane.
 
• It is odorless that's why Ethyl Mercaptan is added to it so there may be a smell if LPG leaks from its storage container.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Water Gas :

 
 
• Water-gas is a mixture of CO and H2.
 
• However, by-products such as char, tar, soot, ash, and condensates are also produced. 
 
 
 
• Natural gas (also called fossil gas; sometimes just gas), is a naturally occurring hydrocarbon gas mixture consisting primarily of methane, but commonly including varying amounts of other higher alkanes, and sometimes a small percentage of carbon dioxide, nitrogen, hydrogen sulfide, or helium.
 
• Compressed natural gas is a fuel that can be used in place of petrol (gasoline), diesel fuel, and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).
 
 
• CNG combustion produces fewer undesirable gases than the aforementioned fuels.
 
• In comparison to other fuels, natural gas poses less of a threat in the event of a spill, because it is lighter than air and disperses quickly when released.

questions.question: Which of following compounds is used as an ingredient in antacids?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium hydrogen carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium hydrogen carbonate, also known as baking soda, is commonly used as an ingredient in antacids.
 
• It helps to neutralize stomach acid, providing relief from heartburn and indigestion.
 
• Antacids containing sodium hydrogen carbonate are effective in treating acid reflux and peptic ulcers.
 
• Sodium hydrogen carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid in the stomach to produce carbon dioxide, water, and salt, reducing acidity.
 
• It is preferred in antacid formulations because it works quickly to relieve symptoms of hyperacidity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrochloric acid**

 
 
• It is a strong acid produced in the stomach to aid in digestion.
 
• Excess production of hydrochloric acid can lead to conditions like acid reflux and ulcers.
 
 
 
• **Calcium carbonate**
 
 
• It is another compound often used in antacids to neutralize stomach acid.
 
• Calcium carbonate is effective in providing longer-lasting relief compared to sodium hydrogen carbonate.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide**
 
 
• Commonly known as milk of magnesia, it is used in antacids to neutralize stomach acid and relieve constipation.
 
• Magnesium hydroxide works by drawing water into the intestines, making it easier to pass stool.

questions.concept: Chemistry in Everyday Life, States of Matter
questions.question: The boiling point of water is _____
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100º C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The boiling point of water is 100º C at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atmosphere).
 
• At this temperature, water transitions from a liquid state to a gaseous state (steam).
 
• The boiling point can vary depending on the atmospheric pressure; it is lower at higher altitudes where the atmospheric pressure is less.
 
• 100º C corresponds to 373.15 K in Kelvin scale.
 
• Boiling point is a physical property of a substance, and it is used to characterize and identify substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Freezing Point of Water**

 
 
• The freezing point of water is 0º C (32º F) at standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• At this temperature, water transitions from a liquid state to a solid state (ice).
 
 
 
• **Melting Point**
 
 
• The melting point of ice is the same as the freezing point of water, which is 0º C (32º F).
 
• At this temperature, ice transitions from a solid state to a liquid state (water).
 
 
 
• **Sublimation**
 
 
• Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas state, without passing through the liquid state.
 
• Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) sublimates at -78.5º C (-109.3º F) at standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: The atomic mass of an element is usually expressed in which of the following units?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic mass units (amu)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atomic mass units (amu) are the standard unit of mass that quantifies the mass of an atom or molecule.
 
• 1 amu is defined as one twelfth (1/12) of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
 
• The atomic mass unit allows chemists to compare the masses of different atoms on a scale that is easy to use and understand.
 
• The unit is widely used in chemistry and physics to express atomic and molecular weights.
 
• Atomic mass units are essential for understanding chemical reactions, molecular structures, and isotopic compositions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes:**

 
 
• Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons and thus different atomic masses.
 
• Examples include Carbon-12, Carbon-13, and Carbon-14.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass:**
 
 
• The mass of one mole of a substance (usually expressed in g/mol).
 
• It is numerically equal to the atomic or molecular mass in amu but expressed in grams.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Number:**
 
 
• The number of atoms, ions, or molecules in one mole of a substance, approximately 6.022 x 10²³.
 
• This constant is used to convert between atomic mass units and grams.
 
 
 
• **Relative Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• A weighted average of the atomic masses of an element's isotopes.
 
• It reflects the abundance of each isotope in nature.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about DNA and RNA is true?

options.text: DNA is not present in viruses.
DNA acts only as a messenger molecule.
RNA has multiple roles including catalytic functions.
RNA acts solely as genetic material in all living organisms.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**RNA has multiple roles including catalytic functions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RNA** is a versatile molecule that performs various functions essential for life.
 
• In addition to being a genetic material in certain organisms (like viruses), RNA also plays a major role in protein synthesis as **messenger RNA (mRNA), transfer RNA (tRNA), and ribosomal RNA (rRNA).**
 
• Certain types of RNA, such as **ribozymes**, exhibit **catalytic functions**. Ribozymes catalyze biochemical reactions, such as cleaving RNA molecules or forming peptide bonds during protein synthesis.
 
• The discovery of catalytic RNA challenged the traditional belief that only **proteins** could act as enzymes.
 
• RNA is involved in processes such as **gene regulation, splicing, and editing**, highlighting its multifunctional nature.
 
• The ability of RNA to fold into complex three-dimensional structures is crucial for its catalytic and regulatory roles.
 
• Examples of RNA molecules with catalytic functions include **self-splicing introns** and the **ribosome**, where rRNA catalyzes peptide bond formation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DNA is not present in viruses**__

 __
 
• Some viruses, such as **retroviruses** (e.g., HIV), use RNA as their genetic material instead of DNA.
 
• However, many viruses, including **adenoviruses and herpesviruses**, contain DNA as their genetic material. Hence, the statement is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **DNA acts only as a messenger molecule**__
 __
 
• DNA is primarily the **repository of genetic information** in most organisms. It does not function as a messenger molecule; this role is performed by **RNA (mRNA).**
 
 
 
• **RNA acts solely as genetic material in all living organisms**__
 
 
• In most living organisms, **DNA** serves as the primary genetic material, while RNA plays supporting roles. Only certain viruses use RNA as their genetic material.

questions.question: Identify the body part that does NOT contain involuntary muscles.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biceps**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Biceps** are voluntary muscles, meaning they are under conscious control.
 
• These muscles are part of the skeletal muscle group, which facilitates movement by attaching to bones.
 
• The primary function of the biceps is to flex the elbow and rotate the forearm.
 
• Skeletal muscles, including the biceps, are striated in appearance due to their fiber structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Involuntary Muscles**:

 
 
• These muscles operate without conscious control.
 
• Examples include muscles found in the heart, digestive system, and respiratory system.
 
• They play essential roles in bodily functions like heartbeats and digestion.
 
 
 
• **Skeletal Muscles**:
 
 
• These are voluntary muscles attached to bones.
 
• They are responsible for body movements and maintaining posture.
 
• Skeletal muscles are characterized by their striated appearance under a microscope.
 
 
 
• **Cardiac Muscle**:
 
 
• The heart muscle is involuntary and striated.
 
• It contracts rhythmically and continuously to pump blood throughout the body.
 
• Unlike other involuntary muscles, cardiac muscle can generate its own electrical impulses.
 
 
 
• **Smooth Muscle**:
 
 
• Found in walls of internal organs like the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels.
 
• These muscles are non-striated and involuntary.
 
• They help in functions such as peristalsis and regulation of blood pressure.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Which of the following is the least reactive metal in the reactivity series?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Au**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gold (Au) is known for its exceptional resistance to corrosion and tarnishing, which is why it is considered the least reactive metal in the reactivity series.
 
• Gold does not react with most acids; it only dissolves in a mixture of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid, known as aqua regia.
 
• Gold is often found in its elemental form in nature, which indicates its low reactivity compared to other metals.
 
• Due to its low reactivity, gold is widely used in jewelry and electronic components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series of Metals**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a series of metals, listed in order of their reactivity, from highest to lowest.
 
• Metals at the top of the series, like potassium, sodium, and calcium, are highly reactive and readily participate in chemical reactions.
 
• Metals at the bottom of the series, such as gold, silver, and platinum, are very unreactive.
 
• The reactivity series is crucial in predicting the outcomes of displacement reactions and understanding the extraction and corrosion processes of metals.
 
 
 
• **Aqua Regia**
 
 
• Aqua regia is a highly corrosive mixture of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid in a molar ratio of 1:3.
 
• It is one of the few reagents capable of dissolving gold and platinum.
 
• The name "aqua regia" means "royal water" in Latin, referring to its ability to dissolve the noble metals.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Gold**
 
 
• Due to its excellent conductivity and resistance to corrosion, gold is widely used in electronics, particularly in connectors and switches.
 
• Gold's malleability makes it ideal for creating intricate jewelry and decorative items.
 
• Gold is also used in dentistry and medicine, particularly in restorative procedures and medical devices.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the effects of changes in pressure on the states of matter?

Statement I: Applying pressure and reducing temperature can liquefy gases.

Statement II: Solid carbon dioxide is stored under high pressure.

options.text: Both statements I and II are correct.
Neither statement I nor II is correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements I and II are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I**: Applying pressure and reducing temperature can liquefy gases.
 
• Liquefaction of gases is a common process used in various industries, such as the production of **liquefied natural gas (LNG)**.
 
• Examples include **carbon dioxide (CO2)** and **oxygen (O2)**, which can be liquefied under high pressure and low temperature.
 
• **Statement II**: Solid carbon dioxide is stored under high pressure.
 
• Solid carbon dioxide is commonly known as **dry ice**.
 
• Dry ice is used in various applications like **preserving perishable items** and creating special effects in movies.
 
• It sublimates directly from solid to gas at normal atmospheric pressure, hence it is stored under high pressure to maintain its solid state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dry Ice**__

 __
 
• **Dry ice** is the solid form of **carbon dioxide (CO2)**.
 
• It is extremely cold, with a temperature of **-78.5°C (-109.3°F)**.
 
• Dry ice is used in **food industry** for shipping perishable products, and in **medical field** for preserving biological samples.
 
• It is also used in **entertainment industry** for creating fog effects.
 
 
 
• **Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG)**__
 
 
• **LNG** is natural gas that has been cooled down to liquid form for ease of storage and transport.
 
• It is typically stored at **cryogenic temperatures** of about **-162°C (-260°F)**.
 
• LNG is used primarily for **energy production** and is a cleaner alternative to other fossil fuels.
 
• Countries like **Qatar, Australia, and the United States** are major producers of LNG.

questions.question: Which of the following acids gives less H+ ions when dissolved in water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CH3**____**COOH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acetic acid** is extremely soluble in water, but most of the dissolved compound remains as molecules, rendering it a **weak electrolyte**. 

 
 
• Acetic acid is extremely soluble in water, but only a small fraction is dissociated into ions, rendering it a weak electrolyte.
 
 
• **It gives less H+ ions when dissolved in water**__.
 
 
 
• **A weak acid** (e.g. CH3COOH) is in equilibrium with its ions in water and its conjugate (**CH₃COO**–, a weak base) is also in equilibrium in water.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitric acid (HNO₃)** decomposes into water, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen, forming a brownish-yellow solution. 

 
 
• It is a strong acid, completely ionized into hydronium (H3O+) and nitrate (NO3−) ions in an aqueous solution, and a powerful oxidizing agent (one that acts as an electron acceptor in oxidation-reduction reactions).
 
 
 
• When **H₂SO₄** is dissolved in water it** dissociates to produce ions.**
 
 
• The H+ ions react with the water molecules to form the hydronium ions.
 
 
 
• When **HCl **molecules dissolve they dissociate into H⁺ ions and Cl⁻ ions.
 
 
• HCl is a strong acid because it dissociates almost completely.

questions.question: The weight of a boy on the surface of the moon is 300 N. The weight of the same boy on the surface of the earth will be ________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Weight of the boy on the surface of the moon = 300 N
 
• The value of g on the moon is 1/6th of the value of g on the earth. As a result, the weight of the boy on the surface of the earth will be **6 times higher of that on the moon**.
 
• The weight of the same boy on the surface of the earth will be: 300 × 6 = **1800 N__**

questions.question: The direction of a magnetic field due to a straight current carrying conductor can be determined using:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right hand thumb rule.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The direction of a magnetic field due to a straight current-carrying conductor can be determined using the **Right-hand thumb rule**.

 
 
• The **Right-hand thumb rule** states that if you hold the current-carrying conductor with your right hand such that the thumb points in the direction of the current, then the fingers wrapped around the conductor will point in the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
• This rule is a practical way to determine the orientation of the magnetic field generated by electric current in a straight conductor.
 
• The magnetic field forms concentric circles around the conductor with the direction given by the right-hand thumb rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's left-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
 
• **Fleming's right-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of induced current when a conductor moves in a magnetic field.
 
• The **Left hand thumb rule** is not commonly used in the context of magnetic fields and current-carrying conductors.
 
• Understanding these rules is crucial for students and professionals working with electromagnetism and related fields.

questions.question: Which of the following tissues is present in stems, around vascular bundles, in the veins of leaves and the hard covering of seeds and nuts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sclerenchyma** is a type of **supportive tissue in plants**, characterized by thickened, lignified cell walls.
 
• It is present in stems, around vascular bundles, in the veins of leaves, and the hard covering of seeds and nuts, providing structural support and strength.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are typically** dead at maturity and provide rigidity and support to the plant**.
 
• This tissue is further divided into two types: **fibers** and **sclereids**, both contributing to the plant's mechanical strength.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apical Meristem**

 
 
• It is a tissue found at the **tips of roots and shoots**, responsible for the primary growth of the plant.
 
• Cells in the apical meristem are undifferentiated and actively divide to allow the plant to grow in length.
 
 
 
• **Epidermis**
 
 
• It is the **outermost layer of cells covering the leaves, flowers, roots, and stems of plants**.
 
• The epidermis serves as a protective barrier against environmental stress and pathogens.
 
 
 
• **Parenchyma**
 
 
• This tissue is composed of living cells that are often involved in** storage, photosynthesis, and tissue repair**.
 
• Parenchyma cells have thin cell walls and are found throughout the plant.
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma**
 
 
• It is a type of plant tissue that **provides support to growing parts of the plant**, such as young stems and leaves.
 
• Collenchyma cells have unevenly thickened cell walls and are typically living at maturity.

questions.question: The average speed of the car on a particular stretch of road is 90 km/hr. On a particular day, the average speed was 1/5 less than on normal days, as a result, it took 16 minutes longer. What is the length (in km) of this particular stretch of road?
questions.solution:
Given:

The average speed on normal days is 90kmph

On a particular day, the average speed was 1/5 less than on normal days and it took 16 minutes i.e. 4/15 hours longer.

Concept used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Let the length of the stretch of the road & time taken on a normal day be D km & H hours respectively.

On that particular day, the average speed = 90 - 90/5 = 72kmph

According to the question,

D = 90 × H ....(1)

D = 72 × (H + (4/15)) ....(2)

So,

90 × H = 72 × (H + (4/15))

⇒ 60H + 16 = 75H

⇒ H = (16/15)

⇒ 90 × H = 90 × (16/15)

⇒ D = 96 (From 1)

**∴ The length of this particular stretch of road is 96 km.**

questions.question: The combination of alleles at specific gene locations on an organism's chromosomes, representing its genetic constitution, is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**genotype**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **genotype** refers to the genetic makeup of an organism. It is the combination of **alleles** at specific gene locations on the organism's chromosomes.
 
• It determines the hereditary characteristics of an organism and remains unchanged throughout its life.
 
• The genotype is represented by specific **letters** or symbols that indicate the alleles present, such as "AA," "Aa," or "aa."
 
• It is a crucial concept in **Mendelian genetics**, where traits are understood based on dominant and recessive alleles.
 
• The genotype interacts with the environment to produce the observable traits or physical expression, known as the **phenotype**.
 
• For example, in pea plants studied by **Gregor Mendel**, the genotype "TT" or "Tt" results in tall plants, whereas "tt" results in short plants.
 
• The study of genotypes is essential in understanding genetic disorders, inheritance patterns, and evolutionary biology.
 
• Modern technologies like **genotyping** and **DNA sequencing** help scientists analyze genotypes for medical and research purposes.

• **DNA**__

 __
 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)** is the molecule that carries the genetic instructions for the development, functioning, growth, and reproduction of all known living organisms.
 
• It is composed of two strands forming a **double helix structure**, discovered by **James Watson and Francis Crick** in 1953.
 
• DNA contains the genetic information in sequences of **nucleotides**, which include adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G).
 
• While the genotype is the combination of alleles, DNA is the physical medium that stores and transmits genetic information.
 
 
 
• **Double Helix**__
 __
 
• The term **double helix** refers to the structure of DNA, consisting of two strands twisted around each other.
 
• It was first described by **Watson and Crick** based on the X-ray diffraction data produced by **Rosalind Franklin**.
 
• The strands are held together by **hydrogen bonds** between complementary bases (A pairs with T, C pairs with G).
 
• While the double helix is a structural property of DNA, the genotype is about the specific genetic information encoded within the DNA.
 
 
 
• **Phenotype**__
 
 
• The **phenotype** refers to the observable physical or biochemical characteristics of an organism, such as height, eye color, or enzyme activity.
 
• It is influenced by both the **genotype** and the environment.
 
• For example, two plants with the same genotype for height might vary in actual height due to differences in **soil quality**, **water availability**, or **sunlight exposure**.
 
• While the genotype is the genetic blueprint, the phenotype represents the expression of that blueprint.
